title: Fetch an owner's needed subset by indexed query, write back only changed records

facts.note: Bun conventions catalog; code may run on Node. Mirrored in given ('TypeScript source').
Non-test source files only; mirrored in given ('not tests').
Mirrors given: a use case or route handler, or the store/adapter method serving that request path.

The trigger: the change writes or edits code that reads a filtered subset of one owner's records (and optionally persists changes to them) from a store that also keeps that owner's history. Applies to new implementations with no existing violation and regardless of task wording. Violation patterns (unscoped reads + in-memory filter, N+1 reads, whole-collection writes) are detection aids listed in verifier_detail, not applicability requirements.

fires: A new use case is being written that returns an owner's currently valid entries; no store query for that exists yet.
A read-only handler loads every record of an owner and filters to the currently valid ones in memory.
A use case sorts an owner's full history in application code to pick the oldest still-open entries, then updates them.
A store adapter method serving a request returns open invoices by linearly scanning all records.
A use case loops over ids and awaits one store `get` per id.
After changing two records, the code saves the owner's entire record list or the whole collection.
doesNotFire: Explicit full-history operations: export, audit report, migration, backfill.
Test files, including fixtures that seed large histories.
Pure domain functions operating on an already-bounded list passed in.
Code reading a single record by id with no owner-subset filtering.

given: In TypeScript source (not tests), a use case or route handler, or the store/adapter method serving it, needs a small filtered subset of one owner's records (e.g. currently valid balance entries, open invoices, active bookings) from a store that also keeps that owner's full history.
when: The code reads that subset and, if it changes any of those records, persists the changes.
then: Fetch only the needed subset via a keyed store query (owner + filter + ordering pushed into the store/adapter) and write back only the records that changed, so store calls and records touched per request do not grow with the owner's history.
prefer: If missing, add a narrow adapter method, e.g. `findValidByOwner(ownerId: string, at: Date): Promise<Entry[]>` ordered by a key, backed by an index or per-owner structure.
Persist by id: `update(id, patch)` per modified record, or `updateMany(changed)`.
avoid: `(await store.all()).filter(r => r.ownerId === id && r.open).sort(...)` in application code.
Adapter query methods that linearly scan all records.
Rewriting the whole collection or every owner record after a few changed.
N+1 reads: `for (const id of ids) await store.get(id)`.
Caching or call-count tricks that pass a test while still scanning history.
unless: The operation's output is the full history itself (export, audit report, migration, backfill).
why: Request cost must track the records actually used, not the owner's age; scans of growing history become latency and memory failures for long-lived owners.
evidence: A test seeds a large history (e.g. thousands of inactive/expired records for one owner) and asserts store calls and records read/written per request are bounded by the records actually used, unchanged as the history grows.

Reviewer sees no full-collection or full-owner read in the request path, no in-memory filter/sort of history in the application layer, no per-record store read inside a loop, and writes keyed by id limited to modified records.
verifier_detail: Detection aid (needs new static observer): in application/route code, flag unscoped store reads (`all`, `list`, `findAll`, `getAll`, owner-wide `findByOwner` without filter) followed by `.filter`/`.sort`/`.find` on the result.

Detection aid: flag awaited per-record store/adapter reads (`get`, `findById`, etc.) inside `for`/`forEach`/`map` loops over records or ids (N+1). Do not flag per-id writes in a loop over only the modified records.
Detection aid: flag writes that replace the whole collection or all owner records (`saveAll`, `replaceAll`, writing the full array back) when only a subset changed.
Optional hint only: task terms such as active, valid, open, current, expire, balance, history may raise reviewer attention; absence of these words does not exempt the change.
Check that a new query method lives in the store/adapter (integration layer) and is backed by an index, keyed map, or per-owner structure, not a linear scan.
Reviewer/LLM judgment (finding): whether store calls and records touched per request grow with history size.

Large-history test threshold: store calls and records read/written per request are O(records actually used) and unchanged when inactive history grows (e.g. same counts at 10 vs 10,000 historical records).
Exempt: test files; explicit full-history operations whose output is the history.
audit: Written for PLT-85 as a new general convention; no canonical source YAML. Derived from spec.md. Round 3: activation trigger is now the subset-read change context (applies to new implementations regardless of wording); violation operations, history-growth findings and task terms moved to verifier_detail as detection aids; given now includes the store/adapter serving the request, consistent with the integration layer in activation.
